cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:03.title: Fire Sprinkler Designer
cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:03.description: Our client is a leader in the fire protection industry. We are looking for a Fire Sprinkler Designer, responsible for producing code-compliant, constructible fire sprinkler system designs from concept through permit approval and construction support. Self-directed designer with deep knowledge of NFPA standards, strong field awareness, and proven experience using AutoSprink and / or Revit in a production environment. This role requires ownership of design quality, coordination, and constructability. Essential Duties & Responsibilities • Design and layout fire protection sprinkler systems—including wet, dry, pre-action, deluge, fire pumps, and tank systems—using specialized CAD software based on the AutoCAD (AutoSprink) and Revit. --AutoSprink experience highly desired. • Coordinate sprinkler system piping with architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical building components. • Perform hydraulic calculations and convert design dimensions into fabrication-ready measurements. • Read and interpret construction documents, including drawings, specifications, and contracts. • Apply applicable NFPA standards based on building type, construction type, hazard classification, and architectural features. • Prepare complete design submittal packages and manage correspondence required to obtain design approvals and permits. • Review work orders, scope sheets, and procedural manuals to determine critical design requirements. • Prepare fabrication lists for pipe fabrication vendors and requisition materials as needed. • Conduct field surveys and field checks to verify design accuracy and suitability for installation. • Assist field personnel with design-related installation questions and resolve design issues during construction. Coordinate with Estimation, Design Management, Operations, and other internal teams to meet project schedules and delivery dates. • Communicate with AHJs, contractors, and other trades to ensure compliance and coordination. • Support permitting and inspection processes, including preparation of required documentation. • Participate in pre-design, coordination, and review meetings. • Identify opportunities for cost savings, efficiency improvements, and quality enhancement. • Prepare and submit final job close-out documents following acceptance testing. • Adhere to company safety policies and maintain a professional, customer-focused approach. Skills & Competencies • 5+ years of fire protection design experience. • Proven experience with AutoSprink or HydraCAD and / or Revit. • NICET Level III–IV certification in Water-Based Systems Layout preferred. • Strong working knowledge of NFPA 13, NFPA 13R, NFPA 13D, and related standards. • Experience with BIM coordination and designing fire sprinkler systems across multiple system types and manufacturers. • Strong understanding of NFPA standards and applicable codes (IFC, IBC, NEC). • Ability to visualize 3D concepts and solve mathematical problems involving geometry and algebra. • Skilled in reading and interpreting architectural, mechanical, and electrical drawings. • Maintain accurate, auditable records and manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment. • Excellent verbal and written communication skills. • Strong attention to detail with emphasis on accuracy and quality. • Ability to obtain and maintain required national, state, and local licenses. • Ability to travel in area as needed.

foundersfactory-founders-factory:ashbyhq.title: CTO & Co-Founder at Insurtech Infrastructure Venture
foundersfactory-founders-factory:ashbyhq.description: Malcolm is building the infrastructure layer for AI-powered insurance distribution: the system that sits between AI agents and insurer APIs, making conversational flows reliable, compliant, and production ready. We’re live with Aviva, we have a small engineering team in place, and we have a clear vision of what we’re working towards. We’re looking for a technical co-founder to take ownership of where we go from here. THE PROBLEM Insurance distribution is changing. The incumbent channel - a price comparison site, a form, and a decision tree, has been dominant for 20 years - but that won’t be the case forever. Not because chatbots are a game-changer in themselves, but because a genuine agent-led flow - one that collects precise, validated data through a natural conversation - can deliver better data quality, a better quote, and a better customer experience than any form ever could. Malcolm is that infrastructure. We sit between the AI agent and the insurer’s quoting API, handling the structured conversation, data validation, enrichment, and submission. WHERE WE ARE Uncommonly at our stage, we’re live at scale in enterprise with room to grow. Malcolm is in production with Aviva for Home and Life insurance, operating through MCP (Model Context Protocol) and 1st party chat experiences. We have a small engineering team, a clear technical roadmap, and a founder who has deep domain and commercial context. What we don’t yet have is the technical co-founder who will shape the architecture of what this becomes at scale. That’s the role. WHAT YOU'LL OWN This is not a “head of engineering” role with a defined brief. As CTO and co-founder, you’ll take full ownership of technical direction: - Define the architecture of the multi-class, multi-insurer platform - a genuinely interesting infrastructure problem at every layer. - Lead the build of our agent-first orchestration engine: the conversational layer that sits at the heart of Malcolm’s differentiation. - Grow and lead the engineering team (currently 1-3 engineers), hiring deliberately as the roadmap demands. - Work directly with insurer partners on integrations - the commercial context matters here and you’ll be in those conversations. - Be a genuine co-founder partner to the CEO: product strategy, commercial decisions, fundraising narrative. WHO YOU ARE You’ve built and shipped production systems. You have strong opinions about architecture and you can defend them. You can write code and you can lead a team that writes code better than you. You’re excited by the specific problem here - not just AI in the abstract, but the precise challenge of making LLM-led conversational flows deterministic enough to operate in a regulated financial services context. You understand why that’s hard. You want to build a company, not just a product. You’ll have real input on commercial and product direction, and you’ll find that energising rather than distracting. You’re London-based, or willing to be. You’re comfortable with early-stage ambiguity and you know the difference between moving fast and moving carelessly in a regulated industry. WHAT WE'RE OFFERING This is a meaningful co-founder stake. You should expect to be a long-term owner of the company, not an early employee with options. The infrastructure layer for AI insurance distribution doesn’t exist yet in any mature form. Malcolm is already in production. The window to define what this category looks like - technically and commercially - is open now. We’re looking for someone who sees that and wants to shape it.

jobDescription.title: CTO & Co-Founder at Insurtech Infrastructure Venture

weloglobal-weloglobal:lever:726af0ac-f4b.description: Overview Welo Data is looking for sharp, curious, and detail-oriented individuals to join our team as Data Labeling Associate. This is not a traditional annotation role. You’ll be working directly with cutting-edge AI systems — evaluating outputs, identifying gaps, and helping improve how these systems behave in real-world scenarios. The work sits at the intersection of data quality, model evaluation, and human judgment, where your ability to think critically matters just as much as following guidelines. We’re looking for people who are naturally curious about AI, comfortable forming opinions, and confident in contributing to conversations with teammates, leads, and stakeholders.
